failure_modes: Assay interference by formulation excipients or device leachables produces apparent loss or alteration of capture-positive signal or protected-cargo readouts, and capture-compatibility controls fail to fully detect or correct for this, leading to false positive "failure" calls.

Capture reagents (antibodies/lipid binders) show variable affinity/epitope accessibility across buffers, lots, or after stress, producing inconsistent co-localization with particle peaks and poor inter-lot reproducibility.

Spike-in intact-EV tracer is unavailable, behaves differently from product EVs, or is unreliable in recovery, preventing valid within-sample normalization and leaving observed changes uninterpretable.

Protected-cargo assays (targeted miRNA/protein panels) lack sensitivity on low-biomass eluates or show high variability across biological lots, so the protected-cargo fingerprint is not reproducible (high uncertainty) and cannot serve as a stability gate.

Bulk particle counts remain unchanged while orthogonal signatures vary unpredictably, making it impossible to set a qualitative pass/fail rule that meaningfully separates acceptable from unacceptable conditions (i.e., no consistent pattern across >=3 lots).

Orthogonal signatures, even if robust in vitro, do not predict in vivo intact-EV recoverable exposure or functional potency (route- and species-specific delivery barriers), so passing the gate does not increase confidence in translational delivery — delivering a false sense of product readiness.

Density/SEC fractionation and fraction-level analyses introduce dilution, adsorption, or loss that differentially affect markers and cargos versus particles, confounding co-localization metrics and protection assays.

Device/shear simulations and matrixed conditions do not reproduce clinically relevant stresses or produce variable stress intensity across replicates, undermining conclusions about "clinically relevant" failure modes.

Regulatory or manufacturing pressure to convert qualitative gates into numeric release limits before sufficient validation leads to inappropriate thresholds or batch rejections based on assay artifacts.
strongest_objection: The single strongest bounded reason this proposal could fail is that observed changes in the proposed orthogonal "intact-EV" signatures are dominated by assay interference or capture-reagent incompatibility (including excipient- or device-derived interference) rather than by true membrane/cargo damage, so the workflow cannot reproducibly discriminate stable vs damaged material across lots and conditions — i.e., the proposed qualitative gate reports assay artifacts, not product stability or intact-EV exposure potential.
